docs.text:
Let's say you are trying to import your Credit Card bill and you want map the transaction to a specific expense account based on the description. You can use the match helper to do that. The helper takes a string and a map of key value pairs. The key is the account to be returned if the string matches the value. The value must be a valid regular expression.

{{match ROW.C Expenses:Shopping="Amazon|Flipkart" Expenses:Groceries="BigBasket"}}

In case of no match null will be returned. You can combine this with or helper to return a default account.

{{or
  (match ROW.C Expenses:Shopping="Amazon|Flipkart" Expenses:Groceries="BigBasket")
  "Expenses:Unknown"
}}

docs.title: Investment
docs.text: The investment page shows your holdings, their market value and a set of yearly cards. Each yearly card summarizes the financial year that starts at financial_year_starting_month and reports how much of your income you did not spend and how much of it you invested.

docs.title: The numbers on a yearly card
docs.text:
Row Meaning Gross Salary Income Postings under Income:Salary Gross Other Income Postings under any other Income: account Tax Postings under Expenses:Tax Net Income Gross Salary Income + Gross Other Income - Tax Net Expense Postings under Expenses: except Expenses:Tax Investment Postings under Assets: (excluding cash, loan-funded buys and stock splits) Total Surplus Net Income - Net Expense Total Savings Rate 100 * Total Surplus / Net Income Investment Rate 100 * Investment / Net Income

Net Income is Paisa's existing income definition: salary plus every other income posting, minus taxes. "Other income" is not limited to earned income; it can also contain interest, dividends or capital gains, so the card must not be read as a purely employment-income statement.

Expenses:Tax is already subtracted from Net Income and is therefore excluded from Net Expense. Taxes are counted exactly once.

docs.title: How to read the rates
docs.text:
Total Savings Rate describes the share of net income that was not spent. Investment Rate describes the share of net income that was moved into investment accounts. The two answers are different questions: money can be saved without being invested, and money can be invested without being saved (for example by moving an existing cash balance into an investment account).

Negative surpluses and rates above 100% are shown as they are. They are not clipped, because clipping would hide a real overspend or a real drawdown of savings. When Net Income is zero or negative, both rates are shown as N/A instead of 0%, because the division would be meaningless.

Total Surplus and Total Savings Rate are also shown as N/A when the period contains no recorded income posting or no recorded expense posting. A period that only records investments, or only one side of the income/expense pair, cannot state what was saved: "spent nothing" and "expenses not recorded" look identical in the ledger. Paisa does not present either case as a confident figure.

The API reports this through has_income_postings and has_expense_postings. overall_savings_rate_available mirrors whether Net Income is positive; the numeric overall_savings_rate is 0 when it is not available, so consumers must check the flag before displaying it.

The card colors follow the common guideline of saving 20 % of net income: a Total Savings Rate of 20 % or more is green, a positive rate below 20 % is amber, and a negative rate is red. Total Surplus is green when positive and red when negative, and negative amounts are shown in red. N/A values stay neutral, so a period without recorded data does not look like a bad year. Investment Rate is not colored: investing is not good or bad by itself and the 20 % guideline does not apply to it. The colors describe recorded postings only; they are not investment advice.

docs.title: What the surplus is not
docs.text:
The surplus is a calculated value derived from the postings recorded in your ledger. It is not the change in your bank balance and not a complete reconciliation to your net worth:

  • Postings that never made it into the ledger are not visible to Paisa.
  • Transfers between your own asset accounts, loan repayments and changes in the market value of your holdings are not split out in this version.
  • The same income and expense postings can already be reflected elsewhere in Paisa's reports; the yearly card is a summary of recorded postings, not a second set of books.

The information tooltip on the card states this as well: the value is calculated from recorded ledger postings and is not the change in bank balance.

docs.title: Complete periods, partial periods and missing activity
docs.text:
Two flags describe the data behind a card:

  • period_complete only says whether the end of the financial year is already over; a year that ends today already counts as complete. A running financial year is labeled (YTD) and should be read as a year-to-date figure, not as a finished year.
  • has_activity only says whether at least one income, expense, tax or investment posting was processed for that period. A period without any such posting is shown as No recorded activity instead of a confirmed zero surplus.

Neither flag proves that the ledger contains every real-world transaction. Paisa can only report what was recorded.

docs.title: Historical figures are not a forecast
docs.text: Past cards describe past recorded postings. They are not a prediction of future income, spending or returns, and they do not carry any investment recommendation.

docs.title: Journal
docs.text:
All your transactions are stored in plain text files called journal. You can organize your transactions into multiple journal files. The journal_path configuration refers your main journal file. The main journal file can refer other journal files using include directive. The include directive supports wildcards * as well. Transactions are sourced only from the main journal file and other journal files included from the main journal file.

include investments.ledger
include expenses/*.ledger

docs.title: Editor
docs.text: Paisa comes with a journal editor. It allows you to edit all the files with the same file extension as your main journal and in the same or sub directories as your main journal.

docs.title: Backup
docs.text:
Paisa tries its best to keep your journal safe. It creates a backup of your journal file every time you save it. The backup file is created with the same name as your journal file with a .backup.{timestamp} extension. You can revert back to old versions of your journal file via the editor. You can also delete the backup files from the editor.

Warning

It is recommended to keep your journal files and paisa.yaml under version control or other backup mechanism. Paisa's backup mechanism is not a replacement for a proper backup. You can ignore paisa.db file from your version control system, the data in db file can be recreated from your journal files.

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: The journal syntax of the features you use normally along with paisa is documented here. Refer ledger documentation for more details.

docs.title: Transaction
docs.text:
2022/01/01 Salary
    Income:Salary:Acme      -100,000 INR
    Assets:Checking          100,000 INR

A transaction should start with a date followed by description. Following that you can have 2 or more postings. The posting line should have at least 2 leading spaces. The account name and the amount should be separated by at least 2 spaces.

docs.title: Commodity
docs.text:
2022/01/07 Investment
    Assets:Checking         -20,000 INR
    Assets:Equity:NIFTY   168.690 NIFTY @ 118.56 INR

commodity cost can be specified using the @ syntax. Here 118.56 is the per unit cost and 168.690 is the quantity you have bought.

docs.title: Comment
docs.text:
2023/07/01 Rent
    ; This is a transaction comment
    Expenses:Rent             15,000 INR
    Assets:Checking   ; This is a posting comment

Any text after ; is treated as a comment. Comment can be at whole transaction level or individual posting level. Comment is also referred as note in many places, both are same.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
2023/07/01 Rent
    ; Recurring: Rent
    Expenses:Rent             15,000 INR
    Assets:Checking

Transactions can be tagged with extra metadata called tags. Tag has two parts: tag name and value. In the above example, Recurring is the name and Rent is the value. Tag should be inside comment.

docs.title: Include
docs.text:
include investments.ledger
include expenses/*.ledger

Include directive can be used to include other journal files. It supports wildcards *.

docs.title: Ledger CLI
docs.text:
Paisa is compatible with ledger, hledger and beancount. By default paisa will try to use ledger, if you prefer to use hledger or beancount instead, change the ledger_cli value in paisa.yaml

# OPTIONAL, DEFAULT: ledger, ENUM: ledger, hledger, beancount
ledger_cli: hledger

Paisa ships with ledger binary. If you use hledger or beancount, make sure that the binaries are installed.

docs.title: Unavailable Features
docs.text: Some of the features that are available in Paisa are not supported by hledger and beancount

docs.title: hledger
docs.text: • Recurring (partial) - hledger supports automated transactions, but it doesn't allow to add only metadata to transaction. So some of the examples in the recurring section will not work with hledger. It's possible to add metadata to transactions manually.

docs.title: beancount
docs.text:
• Budget - budget is based on periodic transactions that is no supported by beancount.

  • Recurring (partial) - beancount doesn't support automated transactions. It's possible to add metadata to transactions manually. Use lowercase for tag name.

  • Search filter in Transactions and Postings pages doesn't support note property.

docs.title: Recurring
docs.text:
Some of the transactions recur on a regular interval and it might be useful to know the next due date for such transactions. Recurring page shows the upcoming or recently missed transactions.

Paisa depends on the posting metadata to identify which transactions are recurring. This metadata can be added in couple of ways. Let's say you pay rent every month and you want to mark it as recurring, a typical journal would like below

2023/07/01 Rent
    Expenses:Rent             15,000 INR
    Assets:Checking

2023/08/01 Rent
    Expenses:Rent             15,000 INR
    Assets:Checking

You can manually tag a posting by adding ; Recurring: Rent.

2023/07/01 Rent
    ; Recurring: Rent
    Expenses:Rent             15,000 INR
    Assets:Checking

2023/08/01 Rent
    ; Recurring: Rent
    Expenses:Rent             15,000 INR
    Assets:Checking

The first part of the metadata before the colon is called tag name. It should be Recurring. The second part is the tag value. This value is used to group transactions.

Tagging each and every posting can be tiresome. Ledger has a feature called Automated Transaction which can make this process simpler.

= Expenses:Rent
    ; Recurring: Rent

The first line is the predicate and the line below it will get added to any matching posting. By default, it will match the posting account name. But you can target other attributes like payee, amount etc. You can find more examples below, more info about predicate is available on Ledger docs

= expr payee=~/^PPF$/
    ; Recurring: PPF

= expr payee=~/Mutual Fund/
    ; Recurring: Mutual Fund

= expr 'account=~/Expenses:Insurance/ and (payee=~/HDFC/)'
    ; Recurring: Life Insurance

= expr 'account=~/Expenses:Insurance/ and !(payee=~/HDFC/)'
    ; Recurring: Bike Insurance

= expr payee=~/Savings Interest/
    ; Recurring: Savings Interest

Tip

Include the automated transactions at the top of the main ledger file. Ledger will apply the rules only to transactions that follow the automated transactions.

docs.title: Period
docs.text:
Paisa will try to infer the recurring period of the transactions automatically, but this might not be perfect. Recurring period can also be explicitly specified via metadata.

= expr payee=~/Savings Interest/
    ; Recurring: Savings Interest
    ; Period: L MAR,JUN,SEP,DEC ?

Let's say your bank deposits the interest on the last day of the last month of the quarter, we can specify like the example above. Paisa editor recognizes period syntax and shows the upcoming 3 schedules right next to period metadata.

┌─────────── day of the month 1-31
│  ┌─────────── month 1-12 or JAN-DEC
│  │  ┌─────────── day of the week 0-6 (Sunday to Saturday)
│  │  │
1  *  ?

The syntax of the period is similar to cron, with the omission of seconds and hours.

Field Allowed values Special characters Day of month 1–31 * , - ? L W Month 1-12 or JAN-DEC * , - Day of week 0-6 or SUN-SAT * , - ? L

* also known as wildcard represents all valid values. ? means you want to omit the field, usually you use it on the day of month or day of week. L means last day of the month or week. , can be used to specify multiple entries. - can be used to specify range. W means the closest business day to given day of month

Multiple cron expressions can be specified by joining them using |. Refer the wikipedia for more information. If you are not sure, just type it out and the editor will show you whether it is valid and the next 3 schedules if valid.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
• Last day of every month ; Period: L * ?
  • 5th every month ; Period: 5 * ?
  • Every Sunday ; Period: ? * 0
  • 1st of Jan and 7th of Feb ; Period: 1 JAN ? | 7 FEB ?
  • Closest business day to the 15th day of every month. ; Period: 15W * ?

Warning

Recurring page will only display a transaction as recurring if there is more than one transaction with the same tag name. If you have only one transaction, wait untill the next transaction is added to see it on the recurring page.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
Sheet is a notepad calculator that computes the answer as you type. It has full access to your ledger and can be used to calculate the answers for a wide variety of financial questions.

Experimental

Sheet is an experimental feature. Give it a try and let me know how it goes, specially what is missing and what can be improved. The syntax and semantics of sheet may change in future releases.

docs.title: Calculator
docs.text:
Sheet can act as a normal calculator. The example below shows how to calculate the monthly EMI for a home loan.

# Home Loan
price = 40,00,000
down_payment = 20% * price
finance_amount = price - down_payment
interest_rate = 8.6%
term = 30

n = term \* 12
r = interest_rate / 12

# EMI

monthly_payment = r / (1 - (1 + r) ^ (-n)) \* finance_amount

````
</div>
<div class="sheet-result sheet-result-1" markdown>
```text
# Home Loan
40,00,000
8,00,000
32,00,000
0
30

360
0
# EMI
24832
````

</div>
</div>

#### Function

Sheets comes with a set of [built-in functions](#functions). You can also define
your own functions. The example below shows how to define a function

<div class="split-codeview">
<div class="sheet" markdown>

```sheet
# Years to Double
years_to_double(rate) = 72 / rate

years_to_double(2)
years_to_double(4)
years_to_double(6)
years_to_double(8)
years_to_double(10)
years_to_double(12)
years_to_double(14)

# Years to Double

36
18
12
9
7
6
5

````
</div>
</div>

#### Query

Query is what makes sheets powerful. It allows you to query your
ledger postings and do calculations on them. The example below shows
how to calculate cost basis of your assets so you can report them to
Income Tax department.

<div class="split-codeview">
<div class="sheet" markdown>

```sheet
# Schedule AL
date_query = {date <= [2023-03-31]}
cost_basis(x) = cost(fifo(x AND date_query))
cost_basis_negative(x) = cost(fifo(negate(x AND date_query)))

# Immovable
immovable = cost_basis({account = Assets:House})

# Movable
metal = 0
art = 0
vehicle = 0
bank = cost_basis({account = /^Assets:Checking/})
share = cost_basis({account =~ /^Assets:Equity:.*/ OR
                    account =~ /^Assets:Debt:.*/})
insurance = 0
loan = 0
cash = 0

# Liability
liability = cost_basis_negative({account =~ /^Liabilities:Homeloan/})

# Total
total = immovable + metal + art + vehicle + bank + share + insurance + loan + cash - liability
````

</div>
<div class="sheet-result sheet-result-3" markdown>
```text
# Schedule AL

# Immovable

25,00,000

# Movable

0
0
0
1,21,402
66,98,880

0
0
0

# Liability

6,21,600

# Total

86,98,682

````
</div>
</div>

## Syntax

#### Number

Sheet allows comma as a separator. `%` is a syntax sugar for dividing
the number by 100. So `8%` is same as `0.08`.

```sheet
100,00
100.00
-100
8%
````

#### Operators

Sheet supports the following operators. `^` is the exponentiation operator.

```sheet
1 + 1
1 - 1
1 * 1
1 / 1
1 ^ 2
#### Variable You can define variables using `=` operator. Variables have to be defined before they are used. 
x = 1
y = 2

z = x + y
#### Function Sheet comes with a set of [built-in functions](#functions). You can also define your own functions. Function definition starts with the function name and then a list of arguments. The body of the function is a single expression. To call a function, use the function name followed by arguments. 
sum(a, b) = a + b

sum(1, 2)
#### Query Query is a first class citizen in sheet. You can think of a query as a list of postings that match the conditions. The query syntax is same as the [search syntax](./bulk-edit.md#search) used in postings and transactions pages. It has to be enclosed inside a `{}`. Query can be treated as any other value, can be passed as an argument, can be assigned to a variable. In fact you can combine two queries using `#!sheet AND` and `#!sheet OR` operator as well. 
query = {account = Expenses:Utilities AND payee =~ /uber/i}

upto_this_fy = {date < [2024-04-01]}
assets = { account =~ /^Assets:.*/ }
liabilities = { account =~ /^Liabilities:.*/ }

assets_upto_this_fy = upto_this_fy AND assets
liabilities_upto_this_fy = upto_this_fy AND liabilities
What is posting? 
2022/01/01 Salary
    Income:Salary:Acme        -100,000 INR
    Assets:Checking            100,000 INR
In the above transaction, there are two postings. A transaction consists of several postings that sum to zero. If you want to know the cost of your checking account, you would use `#!sheet cost({account = Assets:Checking})` #### Comment Sheet supports single line comments starting with `;` or `//`. 
// set x
x = 1
; set y
y = 2

z = x + y // add x and y
## Functions You can find the full list of built-in functions here. This list is very slim as of now, please start a discussion if you want some functions to be added here. #### `#!typescript cost(q: Posting[] | Query): number` Returns the sum of the cost of all the postings. #### `#!typescript balance(q: Posting[] | Query): number` Returns the sum of the current market value of all the postings. #### `#!typescript fifo(q: Posting[] | Query): Posting[]` Returns the list of postings after performing a FIFO adjustment. For example, assume you have 3 postings 
2020/01/01 Buy
    Assets:Bank:Checking   100 USD
2020/02/01 Buy
    Assets:Bank:Checking   100 USD
2020/03/01 Sell
    Assets:Bank:Checking   -50 USD
after FIFO adjustment, you will get the following postings 
2020/01/01 Buy
    Assets:Bank:Checking    50 USD
2020/02/01 Buy
    Assets:Bank:Checking   100 USD
All your sell postings will be adjusted against the oldest buy postings and you will have the remaining buy postings. #### `#!typescript negate(q: Posting[] | Query): Posting[]` Negates the amount and quantity of all the postings. This would be useful when you want to do some calculation on liabilities or income which are negative in nature.

docs.title: User Authentication
docs.text:
You can setup username and password to make sure only you can access the application. Go to Configuration page and expand the User Accounts section. You can click the icon to add a new username and password. Once you save the configuration, you will get logged out if you had not logged in earlier via another account.

It is important to understand that authentication only protects the application user interface. If someone can access your computer and they can access the folder where Paisa stores the ledger and database files, they will be able to view your data.

docs.title: Implementation details
docs.text:
Paisa uses cryptographic hash function sha-256 to convert your password to digest before storing it in the configuration file. This has few implications. No one can look at the configuration file and get the password, this includes you as well. If you forget the password, you can remove the user accounts from configuration file to get back access.

Warning

If you run paisa on a server and access it over public internet, make sure to use it over https and use a strong password. If you run it over plain http, man in the middle attack can be performed to obtain the data including your password.

docs.title: Goals
docs.text:
Goal helps you track your financial objective and progress. You can create a goal for any financial objective you have, such as saving for a vacation, or building an emergency fund or planning for retirement.

Paisa currently supports two types of goals:

  1. Retirement
  2. Savings

More goal types will be added in the future. Feel free to create a discussion if you have any suggestions.

docs.title: Create Goal
docs.text:
To add a new goal, go to the Configuration page and expand the goals section. You would see a list of goal types. Expand the type you want to add and click on the icon to add a new goal. The configuration details are available in the respective goal type pages.

Under Development

Goals is currently under development and you might see changes with every new release. If you want to share feedback, this is a good time to do so.

docs.title: Retirement
docs.text:
Paisa will help you plan your retirement and track your progress. The first part is figuring out what should be your retirement corpus. This will be your target. Instead of specifying the amount explicitly, you can specify your expected yearly expenses and the safe withdrawal rate.

goals:
  retirement:
    - name: Retirement
      icon: mdi:palm-tree
      swr: 3.3
      yearly_expenses: 1100000

If you use paisa to track expenses, instead of specifying the yearly_expenses, you can specify the list of accounts. Paisa will take the average of the last 3 year expenses

goals:
  retirement:
    - name: Retirement
      icon: mdi:palm-tree
      swr: 2
      expenses:
        - Expenses:Entertainment
        - Expenses:Gift
        - Expenses:Insurance
        - Expenses:Misc
        - Expenses:Shopping
        - Expenses:Utilities

Now that the target is specified, you need to specify the list of accounts where you keep your retirement savings.

goals:
  retirement:
    - name: Retirement
      icon: mdi:palm-tree
      swr: 2
      expenses:
        - Expenses:Entertainment
        - Expenses:Gift
        - Expenses:Insurance
        - Expenses:Misc
        - Expenses:Shopping
        - Expenses:Utilities
      savings:
        - Assets:Equity:*
        - Assets:Debt:*

docs.title: Savings
docs.text:
Savings represents a general financial objective that you want to achieve, like buying a car, or a house, or a vacation.

goals:
  savings:
    - name: House
      target: 5000000
      icon: fluent-emoji-high-contrast:house-with-garden
      accounts:
        - Assets:Equity:*
        - Assets:Debt:*

Specify the target amount, and the accounts that you keep the money in.

docs.title: Forecast
docs.text:
When you save towards an objective, you will have a target date in mind. In the below config, you are specifying the target date and rate. Paisa will calculate the monthly contribution required to achieve the goal.

goals:
  savings:
    - name: House
      target: 5000000
      target_date: 2030-05-01
      rate: 10
      icon: fluent-emoji-high-contrast:house-with-garden
      accounts:
        - Assets:Equity:*
        - Assets:Debt:*

If on the other hand, you know how much you can afford to save every month, but want to know when the goal will be achieved, you can specify the payment per period and the rate. Paisa will calculate the target date.

goals:
  savings:
    - name: House
      target: 5000000
      payment_per_period: 50000
      rate: 10
      icon: fluent-emoji-high-contrast:house-with-garden
      accounts:
        - Assets:Equity:*
        - Assets:Debt:*

docs.title: Math
docs.text:
This section will give some rough idea of how the calculations are done. You can skip this section if you are not interested in the math.

F V + P V × ( 1 + R A T E ) N P E R + P M T × ( 1 + R A T E ) N P E R − 1 R A T E = 0 FV + PV \times (1+RATE)^{NPER} + PMT \times \frac{(1+RATE)^{NPER} - 1}{RATE} =0

Where

Variable Description Paisa FV Future Value target PV Present Value Current Savings PMT Payment per period payment_per_period / Monthly Investment needed RATE Rate of return rate NPER Number of periods target_date

Out of the 5 variables, if you know any 4, the 5th can be calculated by solving the equation. You can refer the blog post for more details.

docs.title: Tax
docs.text: Paisa provides few features to help with tax filing and tax optimization.

docs.title: Supported paths
docs.text:
• india tax regime: tax harvesting, capital gains, and Schedule AL.
  • germany tax regime: capital income reporting with annual allowance, capital income tax, solidarity surcharge, and optional church tax.
  • germany tax regime: annual tax overview with deductible-expense candidates grouped by return section, coverage checks, raw Anlage KAP values and CSV export.

docs.title: Disclaimer
docs.text: The author of this tool is not an accountant, the calculations are made based on their interpretation of rules and regulation. This tool is distributed free hoping it would be useful. The users are advised to consult a tax accountant before making any decision based on the information provided here. Check the LICENSE of paisa for more details.

docs.title: Capital Gains
docs.text:
This page is available for the india tax regime.

Mutual Funds are considered as capital asset and capital gains tax will be charged on any gains. Capital Gains page shows the financial year wise capital gains tax based on the withdrawal transaction. The sum total, account wise breakdown, and per buy/sell match information are available.

Only commodities with tax_category are considered. Please check Tax Harvesting page for configuration details.

docs.title: Gain
docs.text: The difference between the purchase and sell price.

docs.title: Taxable Gain
docs.text:
The gain after applying Indexation or Grandfathering provision.

Based on the duration between the purchase and sell date, an asset might be classified as Short Term or Long Term.

docs.title: Short Term Tax
docs.text: This would be a percentage of the Taxable Gain. The percentage varies based on the asset class.

docs.title: Long Term Tax
docs.text: This would be a percentage of the Taxable Gain. The percentage varies based on the asset class.

docs.title: Taxable at Slab Rate
docs.text:
There are cases where the gain would be added to taxable income and charged Slab rate. Since the tax rate would depend on the person, the whole taxable amount is shown instead of the tax. You can multiply this with your slab rate to get the tax amount.

If you are using the germany tax regime, use the Capital Income page instead.

docs.title: Capital Income
docs.text:
This page is available for the germany tax regime.

Paisa provides a Germany-focused capital income report for realized investment gains. The report summarizes calendar-year realized gains and applies the configured Germany tax inputs from germany_tax.

docs.title: What the report shows
docs.text:
• gross realized gains and realized losses from matched buy and sell lots
  • partial exemption adjustment for commodities that declare germany_partial_exemption_rate
  • taxable amount before and after annual allowance
  • annual allowance used
  • capital income tax
  • solidarity surcharge
  • optional church tax
  • withholding tax paid through broker tax postings
  • tax credit used against the computed annual tax
  • net tax due after available tax credits

The report also surfaces diagnostics when Paisa sees Germany tax activity that may require manual review. Current diagnostics focus on:

  • mutual funds or ETFs with Germany tax activity but no configured germany_partial_exemption_rate
  • dividend or interest income without matching Expenses:Broker:Taxes inputs for the same tax year

The current implementation is intended as a practical first-pass personal investor report. It does not yet model every Germany tax edge case.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The following configuration values control the report:

tax_regime: germany
germany_tax:
  annual_allowance: 1000
  capital_income_tax_rate: 0.25
  solidarity_surcharge_rate: 0.055
  church_tax_rate: 0

commodities:
  - name: VWCE
    type: mutualfund
    price:
      provider: com-yahoo
      code: VWCE
    germany_partial_exemption_rate: 0.3

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The report uses calendar years, which aligns with Germany tax reporting.
  • The allowance is applied at the annual summary level, not per account.
  • Expenses:Broker:Taxes postings are treated as withholding-tax-aware inputs and reduce the remaining annual tax due up to the computed gross tax amount.
  • If germany_partial_exemption_rate is not configured for a mutual fund or ETF, Paisa currently treats the position as fully taxable and emits a warning.
  • India-only workflows such as Tax Harvesting and Schedule AL are not shown in the Germany regime.

docs.title: Germany Tax Overview
docs.text:
This page is available for the germany tax regime. Open it from Tax → Overview; the preview tree has the same page at /preview/tax/overview.

The page is a handover sheet for the German income tax return. It lists ledger candidates grouped by the form section they belong to. It is not a tax calculator and not a confirmed deduction list.

docs.title: What the page is and is not
docs.text:
• It shows postings that match an account rule or carry a tax_category tag.
  • It does not apply tax law: no Arbeitnehmer-Pauschbetrag, no zumutbare Belastung, no 20 % credit, no allowance and no partial-deduction math. Your tax software does that.
  • It does not edit postings.
  • It does not guess from payee names.

docs.title: Year selection
docs.text: The selector lists every year that has postings in the ledger, plus the previous calendar year. It defaults to the previous calendar year. A valid four-digit year between 1900 and 2100 is accepted even when it has no postings; the page then shows empty sections.

docs.title: Sections and categories
docs.text:
Sections are always shown in this order. Empty sections are collapsed and labelled Keine Buchungen.

docs.title: Tagging postings
docs.text:
tax_category on the expense posting is the canonical form.

ledger and hledger:

2025/09/09 * PayPal ; Bürostuhl
    Assets:Checking:ING                      -699,00 EUR
    Expenses:Household:Goods                  699,00 EUR ; tax_category: work_equipment

beancount:

2025-09-09 * "PayPal" "Bürostuhl"
  Assets:Checking:ING       -699.00 EUR
  Expenses:Household:Goods   699.00 EUR
    tax_category: "work_equipment"

A tag on another posting in the same transaction (for example the bank line) is accepted only when the transaction has exactly one expense posting. With zero or several expense postings the page emits a diagnostic instead of guessing. A tag on a split transaction must therefore sit on the relevant expense posting.

To exclude a posting that an account rule would match, tag it with tax_category: "none". The posting is then shown in neither the sections nor the coverage row.

The legacy TaxRelevant tag is never applied. In ledger and hledger, postings that still carry it are reported in a diagnostic and must be migrated to tax_category manually. Legacy values are not category keys: TaxRelevant: Auto and TaxRelevant: Work are personal markers, not valid tax_category values. Replace the tag name and choose a key from the table above:

2025/06/02 * ADAC ; Mitgliedschaft
    Assets:Checking:ING                       -41,00 EUR ; tax_category: work_other
    Expenses:Car:Memberships                   41,00 EUR

2025/09/09 * PayPal ; Bürostuhl
    Assets:Checking:ING                      -699,00 EUR ; tax_category: work_equipment
    Expenses:Household:Goods                  699,00 EUR

The tag may stay on the bank line when the transaction has exactly one expense posting. Put it directly on the expense posting when a transaction splits the expense across several accounts.

docs.title: Account rules
docs.text:
Account matching is configured with tax_deductions.accounts:

tax_deductions:
  accounts:
    - account: Expenses:Health:Insurance
      category: health_insurance
    - account: Expenses:Health
      category: health
    - account: Expenses:Insurance
      category: other_insurance
    - account: Expenses:Tax:Preparation
      category: tax_advice
  • Omitting tax_deductions uses the built-in rules shown above.
  • An explicit list replaces the defaults.
  • An empty list disables account matching; tags still work.
  • Matching is whole-segment prefix matching: Expenses:Health matches Expenses:Health and Expenses:Health:*, but never Expenses:HealthSomething. The longest matching rule wins.
  • Only Expenses: accounts and concrete account names are accepted; wildcards are rejected by configuration validation.
  • Unknown category values are rejected when the configuration is loaded.

These accounts are deliberately not mapped by default: Expenses:Household:*, Expenses:Sports:*, Expenses:Car:*, Expenses:Transportation, Expenses:Phone, Expenses:Utilities:* and Expenses:Travel:*. Tag them explicitly when they are relevant.

docs.title: Coverage
docs.text: The collapsed coverage row counts expense postings in the selected year that were not matched by a tag, the sibling rule or an account rule. It groups them by account. It never shows amounts or individual transactions: most of those postings are private spending, and the row describes the limit of automatic classification, not a list of suspected deductions.

docs.title: Negative postings
docs.text: A negative expense posting (a refund or correction) is included and reduces the category total. It carries a Negativ marker. Paisa does not move it to another year and does not link it to an earlier expense. When the selected year contains negative matched postings, a neutral diagnostic asks you to review the correct tax-year treatment manually.

docs.title: Capital income (Anlage KAP)
docs.text:
The capital income card is separate from the expense sections. Every value is a raw ledger aggregate: aus dem Ledger, kein Steuererklärungswert. None of the values is guaranteed to be a specific Anlage KAP line.

  • Berechnet: realized gains and realized losses from matched buy/sell pairs, split per pair. Losses are shown as a positive number.
  • Gebucht: dividends from Income:Dividend*, interest from Income:Interest*, and booked taxes from Expenses:Broker:Taxes*. The label is Gebuchte Steuern (Art nicht klassifiziert) because Paisa cannot distinguish foreign withholding from German capital gains tax.

Dividends are not grossed up. If a year has dividend or interest income but no Expenses:Broker:Taxes postings, a diagnostic notes that the booked amount may be net of withholding tax. The card never renders a combined capital-income total, and the summary keeps booked capital income and realized gains/losses as separate figures.

docs.title: CSV export
docs.text:
CSV exportieren downloads the selected year as UTF-8 CSV with a BOM. Columns:

section,category,date,payee,account,amount,source,note,file,line

source is tag, transaction or account, and empty for capital income rows. Capital income rows use section=capital_income and keep the raw-value note in the note column. The CSV contains the same raw values as the page, not tax-return field values.

docs.title: Visibility
docs.text: The page and the menu entry are gated by tax_regime: germany. They are independent of locale; locale only controls number and date formatting. Page content is German because the labels are the legal terms used in the German return. Navigation, API fields and code identifiers stay English.

docs.title: Schedule AL
docs.text:
This page is available for the india tax regime.

As per the Indian Income tax law, citizens are obligated to report their entire Assets and Liabilities if the total income exceeds ₹50 lakh. Paisa helps with the computation of the amount.

All you need to do is to specify the accounts that belong to each section. Paisa will compute the total as on the last day of the previous financial year.

docs.title: Tax Harvesting
docs.text:
This page is available for the india tax regime.

Gains from asset types like Mutual Fund, Stock are subject to capital gains tax. The taxation rate itself differs based on how long you hold your investment, whether it's debt or equity, whether you have more than 1 Lakh gains in a year etc. To further complicate things, there might be exit load applicable.

Paisa takes a generic approach and let the user configure when a commodity is safe to harvest. There are two fields related to tax harvesting.

  1. harvest - specifies the number of days after which the commodity is eligible for tax harvesting. This should be set based on fund exit load, fund category etc

  2. tax_category - This defines how the taxes are calculated as the government usually tweaks the tax code regularly with various rules like grandfathering, cost inflation index adjustment, etc.

  3. equity65 - This is for 65% or more investment in Indian equity.

  4. equity35 - This if for 35% or more investment in India equity but less than 65%

  5. debt - This is for debt funds.

  6. unlisted_equity - This is for unlisted foreign on Indian equity.

commodities:
  - name: NIFTY
    type: mutualfund
    code: 120716
    harvest: 365
    tax_category: equity65
  - name: ABSTF
    type: mutualfund
    code: 119533
    harvest: 1095
    tax_category: debt

The tax harvest page will show the list of accounts eligible for harvesting.

docs.title: Multiple Folios
docs.text: Paisa uses FIFO method within an Account. If you have multiple folios, this might result in incorrect values. The issue can be solved by using a different Account for each folio.

docs.title: Paisa-Fork-Review – Stand 25.10.2026
docs.text: Frage: Welche Forks von ananthakumaran/paisa hatten in den letzten sechs Monaten neue Commits, was wurde dort geändert, und welche Themen/Commits sind für unseren Fork (Aerics84/paisa) relevant und sollten übernommen werden?

docs.title: Kurzfazit
docs.text:
• 36 Forks hatten seit dem 25.04.2026 Pushes – inklusive unserem eigenen (Aerics84/paisa). Von den 35 anderen sind 34 erreichbar (sandeepbazar/paisa ist inzwischen 404).
  • 22 der 34 erreichbaren Fremd-Forks enthalten eigene Commits, die nicht in upstream/master sind. 7 haben nur den Upstream-Stand synchronisiert, 3 nur einen Sync-Merge ohne neue eigene Arbeit, 2 nur Bot-Branches (Dependabot/ImgBot).
  • Vier Forks tragen den Großteil der Arbeit: nextxm (309 eigene Commits), Sarath234 (142 + Branch-Arbeit), 1Feng (136) und Pratap-kute (69). Nur die ersten drei enthalten für uns direkt verwertbare Änderungen; Pratap ist ein weitgehender Stack-Umbau (Deno/ECharts, ohne Bulma/D3) und für uns nicht als Ganzes übernehmbar.
  • Der größte unmittelbare Nutzen liegt nicht in den großen Feature-Branches, sondern in etwa 15 kleinen Korrektheits- und Robustheits-Commits: Zeitzonen/Datum, hledger-acost, FilterByGlob, Gehaltsklassifikation, interne Transfers, Yahoo-Crumb/GBp, Tooltips, Template-/Import-Fehler, SQLite-WAL, Backup-Pruning, Preis-Cache/XSS.
  • Für den laufenden Monatsrückblick liefern Sarath (Insights, effektiver Monat, Segment-Sankey) und nextxm (Net-Worth-Konsistenz, FX, Monatsvergleich) wertvolle Ideen und Tests. Eine 1:1-Übernahme verbietet sich aber, weil unsere Spezifikation strenger ist (TWR, Kursfrische, keine erfundenen Nullen, keine falschen Erfolgszustände).
  • Nicht übernehmen: Indien-/China-spezifische Scraper und Importe, SMS-/Gmail-/Telegram-Agenten, Kite/Coin-Integrationen, Deno/ECharts-Komplettumbau, MCP/LLM-Spielereien, der nextxm-Architekturumbau (Auth/SQLc/Connect/Job-Queue) als Ganzes.

docs.title: Methode und Datenstand
docs.text:
• GitHub-API /repos/ananthakumaran/paisa/forks?per_page=100&sort=newest (222 Forks), Filter auf pushed_at >= 2026-04-25 → 36 Forks.
  • Für jeden Fork: Vergleich master...<owner>:<default_branch> gegen upstream/master (18ecd7d, 21.10.2026), zusätzlich Prüfung aller Branches per git ls-remote und Branch-Compares. Reine Upstream-Sync-Merges werden nicht als eigene Arbeit gezählt.
  • „Eigene Commits“ = Commits, die nicht in upstream/master enthalten sind. Bei großen, rebasten Forks (nextxm) gibt es dieselben Änderungen teils unter mehreren SHAs; die Zahlen sind daher Näherungen.
  • Für die inhaltliche Bewertung wurden alle eigenen Commits der aktiven Forks angesehen, nicht nur die seit dem Stichtag. Die Spalte „6 Mon.“ zählt ausschließlich die Commits im Fenster; einzelne empfohlene Fixes (z. B. FilterByGlob, Verschlüsselung) sind älter, stehen aber in Forks, die im Fenster aktiv waren.
  • Unser Stand: master = f738e0c (25.10.2026) auf Basis von upstream v0.7.8, mit laufender Monatsrückblick-Arbeit (internal/server/monthly_review.go, src/lib/monthly_review.ts). Die Empfehlungen sind mit diesem laufenden Arbeitsstand abzugleichen.
  • Zeilennummern in diesem Dokument sind Orientierung; durch die laufende Monatsrückblick-Arbeit können sie sich verschieben. Maßgeblich sind die genannten Funktionen/Dateien.

docs.title: Unser Ausgangspunkt (nicht erneut bauen)
docs.text:
Damit die Empfehlungen nicht Doppelarbeit erzeugen, hier der relevante Ist-Stand unseres Forks:

  • /preview mit Net-Worth-, Checking-, Expense-, Insight- und Goal-Modulen; klassisches Dashboard bleibt separat.
  • Gesamt-Sparquote vs. Investitionsquote (V1) auf den Investment-Jahreskarten.
  • Laufender Monatsrückblick: internal/server/monthly_review.go, monthly_performance.go, src/lib/monthly_review.ts (Flow-Graph, Nettoeinkommens-Trend, Top/Flop-Performance, Checking-Historie).
  • Jahres- und Monats-Sankey, Germany/EU-Import-Templates (CAMT, Trade Republic, Scalable, Germany Broker) und Germany-Tax-Code.
  • Svelte 5, Bulma 1, D3, Go/GORM/SQLite; keine Cloud-/Bank-Sync-Abhängigkeit.

Viele Fork-Features (z. B. Saraths Insights, nextxms Monats-Widgets, Prataps Allocation-UI) überschneiden sich damit. Übernommen werden deshalb primär Korrektheits- und Randfall-Verbesserungen, nicht komplette UI-Module.

docs.text: Die Reihenfolge ist bewusst: zuerst Korrektheit unserer Zahlen (besonders für den laufenden Monatsrückblick), dann Robustheit/Performance, dann UI-Politur.

docs.title: P1-01 Zeitzonen- und Datums-Korrektheit
docs.text:
Commits

  • matthiasdebernardini/paisa@ef719408 – „transaction dates render/export one day off in other timezones“ (06.06.2026)
  • panuozzo77/paisa@67a2fa8a – gleicher Dayjs-Fix für Monatscharts (06.06.2026)

Was

  • utils.Now() läuft in config.TimeZone() statt in der Server-Zeitzone; neue BeginningOfDay()-Hilfe.
  • RunningBalance normalisiert den Starttag, damit Postings am Tagesrand nicht in den falschen Bucket fallen.
  • ajax() parst Datumsstrings als Kalendertag (value.slice(0, 10)), nicht als vollen Instant.
  • CSV-Export nutzt format("YYYY-MM-DD") statt toISOString().

Warum bei uns

  • Unser Default-Profil ist Europe/Berlin (internal/config/config.go:246), aber utils.Now() nutzt time.Now() (internal/utils/utils.go:129). Im Docker-/UTC-Betrieb ist „heute“ damit falsch.
  • RunningBalance startet mit postings[0].Date ohne Normalisierung (internal/accounting/accounting.go:164).
  • ajax() konvertiert 2026-06-06T00:00:00+02:00 in die Browser-Zeitzone (src/lib/utils.ts:915); der Export nutzt toISOString() (src/lib/export.ts:8). Das ist genau der Off-by-one-Fehler, der deutsche Nutzer trifft.
  • Betrifft Monatsrückblick, Net-Worth-Timeline, Cashflow, CSV-Export und Regressionstests.

Ziel bei uns: internal/utils/utils.go, internal/accounting/accounting.go, src/lib/utils.ts, src/lib/export.ts. Tests mit Grenzpostings um 00:00 Europe/Berlin und Browser in UTC.

Aufwand/Risiko: S, niedrig. 67a2fa8a ist im Wesentlichen derselbe Fix; nur einmal übernehmen.

docs.title: 6. Hinweise zum Übernehmen
docs.text:
• Cherry-Pick: git fetch https://github.com/<fork>.git <sha> und git cherry-pick -x <sha>. -x dokumentiert die Herkunft; Paisa ist AGPL-3.0, unser Fork steht unter derselben Lizenz.
  • Keine Merge-Commits übernehmen; immer die eigentlichen Feature-/Fix-Commits.
  • Branch-only-Arbeit (z. B. matthias, stan-ely, coffmant, d093w1z, Sarath-Feature-Branches) per SHA oder Branch fetchen. GitHub erlaubt git fetch <url> <sha> für erreichbare Commits.
  • Konflikte erwarten: Unser Baum ist gegenüber Juni/Juli 2026 deutlich weiter (Svelte 5, Bulma 1, Monatsrückblick, Deutschland/EU). Kleine Patches manuell portieren; Tests aus dem Fork mitnehmen und an unsere Fixtures anpassen.
  • Sarath 6b730f51: unbedingt den Endstand inkl. fdb5c1eb nehmen; der Zwischenstand hat einen Compile-/Logikfehler.
  • nextxm: viele Commits sind rebast/dupliziert. Nicht den Branch mergen; einzelne commits über git show prüfen. Die Struktur (dcPricesTree, Rate-Cache) existiert bei uns nicht.
  • 1Feng: Der Master enthält viele Merge- und China-Commits; nur die genannten Einzelcommits picken.
  • Verifikation: go test ./..., npm run check, npm run test:prepush, npm run test:regression; bei Preis-/Datumsänderungen zusätzlich die Deutschland/EU-Fixtures neu prüfen.

docs.title: 8. Offene Punkte für uns
docs.text:
• Saldo-/Gehaltsdefinition: Wollen wir salary_income_accounts als Config (1Feng) oder eine breitere Heuristik (Sarath: „salary“ im Kontonamen)? Die Config ist expliziter und testbar; die Heuristik ist bequemer, aber fehleranfälliger. Empfehlung: Config, Default Income:Salary + Income:Payroll.
  • Transfer-Globs: Welche Konten sind bei unseren Nutzern typische interne Transfers? Ohne Defaults (transfer_accounts: []) bleibt das Verhalten unverändert; wir brauchen eine Dokumentation mit Beispielen (Assets:Tagesgeld, Assets:Depot:Verrechnung).
  • Yahoo-Crumb: Ist der zusätzliche Cookie-/Crumb-Tanz in unserer Umgebung nötig, oder reicht der GBp-Fix? Vor der Implementierung einen kleinen Netzwerktest mit LSE-/US-Tickern machen.
  • Monatsrückblick-Insights: Welche Sarath-Insights sind mit unserer TWR-/Frische-Spezifikation vereinbar? Nicht einfach die UI übernehmen; zuerst die Datenregeln abgleichen.
  • Rebalancing/Projektion: Beide sind P2, aber sie konkurrieren um dieselbe Allocation-/Goals-UI. Erst nach dem Monatsrückblick entscheiden.
